subject: Clarify: jurisdictional data paths and dedicated-cluster isolation
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@nexabank.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: sec-ops@nexabank.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on dedicated cluster residency, backups, and deletion proof

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — NexaBank team had a couple of follow-ups about Dedicated deployments. Two quick items we need clarified before we move to PO: 

1) Jurisdictional data paths: Can you confirm whether any control-plane logs, billing records, or third-party monitoring (Datadog/Prometheus) sinks for our Dedicated cluster ever transit outside our pinned country? We need a statement for our InfoSec review.

2) Backups & snapshots: What regions are persistent snapshots written to? Are cross-region replicas enabled by default for Dedicated? We need a guaranteed in-region retention and a way to verify deletion when requested.

3) Evidence: For our procurement team, a short list of artifacts that demonstrate deletion (e.g., snapshot-tombstone logs, wipe runbook steps) would be great.

Appreciate concise answers so we can close our security checklist.

— Priya
Priya Shah
Head of Cloud Security, NexaBank
priya.shah@nexabank.com

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@nexabank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on dedicated cluster residency, backups, and deletion proof

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear list. Short answers below; attaching a runbook and a backup matrix for detail.

1) Jurisdictional data paths: Control plane telemetry and billing events are processed in the private control plane you subscribe to for Dedicated. For country-pinned Dedicated, the control plane endpoints and long-term storage for those artifacts remain in the selected country/region. Short-lived operational metrics (aggregate host telemetry for autoscaling) are scrubbed of customer identifiers before any cross-region transmission; we do not route raw tenant blobs outside the pinned jurisdiction.

2) Backups & snapshots: Persistent disk snapshots for tenant volumes are, by default, stored in the tenant's pinned region. Cross-region replication is an opt-in configuration we do not enable without explicit customer consent. See the attached in-region-backup-matrix.xlsx for retention windows and default replica behavior.

3) Evidence of deletion: We produce tombstone entries and a snapshot-deletion audit record (timestamped, signed by the runtime orchestrator) which is available on request. Operational proof can include: (a) snapshot deletion log lines, (b) snapshot tombstone manifest (SHA + timestamp), and (c) a redaction report from the storage subsystem.

Ben, can you add any implementation notes about KV caches and ephemeral artifacts? Marissa, can you confirm the SOC/attestation language we normally provide to customers for this flow?

Next steps: If that aligns, I can schedule a short run-through demo with your SecOps to show the deletion workflow.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Attachments: isolation-runbook.pdf (PDF), in-region-backup-matrix.xlsx (XLSX)

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@nexabank.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 12:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on dedicated cluster residency, backups, and deletion proof

Hi Priya — Ben from Infrastructure here. A few technical clarifications: 

- KV and inference caches: KV caches (model KV cache) and worker-local ephemeral caches are resident on local disks in the tenant's dedicated nodes and are not replicated off-node. They are evicted on instance termination and we run zero-fill passes when disks are returned to the pool. For additional assurance we can enable an encrypted ephemeral volume and provide the key-wrapping logs showing key deletion on wipe.

- Snapshots: Snapshots are point-in-time copies of block volumes. For Dedicated with country pinning we store snapshots in the same region; snapshot deletion creates a tombstone and enqueues secure-delete jobs which zero out blocks and update the snapshot manifest. Those secure-delete jobs produce audit events with job-ids you can reference.

- Monitoring/metrics: We ship metrics to your customer-owned monitoring endpoints if you configure them; otherwise platform metrics retained by Redwood are aggregated and retained in-region for N days (configurable), then rotated. We can provide an endpoint-level data flow diagram as part of the evidence package.

I can demo the secure-delete job logs and key-wrapping teardown in a short ops call.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@nexabank.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on dedicated cluster residency, backups, and deletion proof

Hi Priya — Marissa from Customer Success. Adding the compliance angle: 

- SOC/Security attestations: For Dedicated we provide SOC2 Type II reports and a tailored attestation letter that describes the region-pinning commitments. We don’t include tenant-level artifact exports in the public SOC report, but we will provide an attestation letter and an operations checklist that references the secure-delete job ids and retention windows.

- Evidence package: Typical package includes (1) isolation-runbook.pdf (what we followed), (2) snapshot-deletion-manifest.csv, (3) storage audit logs for the timeframe requested, and (4) a short video screen capture running the deletion job and showing the audit event. We redact operator usernames in the delivery artifact per privacy rules.

If you share acceptable evidence items or an acceptance checklist, we’ll prepare that package.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@nexabank.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: sec-ops@nexabank.com, dlegal@nexabank.com
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on dedicated cluster residency, backups, and deletion proof

Thanks — helpful. Two additional asks before we sign: 

A) We need a short (1-page) plain-language statement we can attach to our procurement file that says: "Redwood will not replicate customer tenant snapshots or raw tenant data outside NexaBank's pinned jurisdiction unless explicitly authorized by NexaBank in writing." Can you provide this as an attested statement?

B) For the deletion workflow we need the following evidence items for one sample purge (test tenant): tombstone manifest, secure-delete job log, and confirmation that no cross-region replica existed for that snapshot. Can you produce these as redacted artifacts?

If you can supply A and B, procurement will issue the PO next week.

— Priya

Priya — thanks for the quick turnaround. Summary / proposed next steps: 

1) Redwood to provide a signed attestation paragraph (one page) that we will not replicate tenant snapshots or raw tenant data outside the pinned jurisdiction without written authorization. Laura will circulate the legal addendum today.

2) Redwood Infra to prepare a redacted evidence package for a sample purge (tombstone manifest + secure-delete job log + replica check). Ben will own the artifact collection; Marissa will coordinate redaction and delivery.

3) Ops walkthrough: Schedule a 30-minute demo with your SecOps to show the deletion workflow and the audit events.

4) Procurement: Once A+B delivered and legal sign-off, NexaBank to issue PO.

I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the Ops walkthrough. Appreciate the collaboration — we’ll treat this as high-priority.

— Jonas
